subject: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexbank.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finexbank.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup

Samir — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Key items we heard: 
- Primary use case: customer support triage + suggested replies for high-touch retail banking customers (sensitive PII handling requirement).
- Success metrics: 85% acceptable reply rate (human-eval), <250ms p50 inference latency for 512 tokens workload, and clear auditability for regulatory review.
- Traffic profile: 200 qps peak burst across 3 regions, mostly US east/west.

Recommended immediate next steps (agreed on call):
1) Run a customer-specific evaluation on Redwood using a ~2k-example dataset you provide (we discussed a 70/30 split: 1.4k in-scope test, 600 edge cases).
2) Redwood to propose model shortlist and baseline benchmarks, with prompt templates and scoring rubric.
3) If baseline looks good, schedule a week-long sandbox on Redwood Dedicated for throughput testing and latency SLO validation.

Please confirm: Asha will share the eval dataset (anonymized) and a few representative prompt templates by EOD Wednesday. I've looped in Neha (on our Eval team) and Dev (infra) to scope setup and scoring.

Attachments: redwood_eval_instructions.pdf (setup checklist, dataset format, scoring guidance)

Thanks — looking forward.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finexbank.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming: Asha will send the anonymized CSV by EOD Wednesday (we're redacting PII per our compliance checklist). A couple clarifications before we hand off to your eval team: 

- Scoring: for suggested replies we typically use a 3-point rubric (OK/Needs Edit/Bad). Can your rubric map to that and also provide a continuous quality score for regression detection?
- Latency: the <250ms p50 is a target but we need percentile visibility (p50/p90/p99) across our sandbox runs.
- Logging/audit: we need token-level logs for the audit team (with redaction of any residual PII) — is that supported on the sandbox?

If you can confirm those, we'll share the dataset. Also, tell Neha we'll include a column with the expected reply and an evaluation hint (gold label) where available.

Samir
Director, Conversational AI — FinEx Bank
samir.shah@finexbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexbank.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@finexbank.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup

Looping you both in to pick this up — Samir/Asha are ready to share the dataset. High level asks: map their 3-point rubric to our continuous scoring and run baseline evals across 3 model variants. Please see attached instructions.

Neha — can you outline the evaluation plan (dataset format expectations, scoring mapping, recommended model shortlist, and estimated turnaround)?
Dev — can you confirm sandbox provisioning steps and what logs we can surface to their audit team?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexbank.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@finexbank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup — Eval plan & dataset spec

Hi Samir / Asha / Marissa — thanks for the handoff. Plan below for the FinEx eval run and what we'll need from your side.

1) Dataset format (please use the attached finex_eval_dataset.csv template):
   - CSV columns: example_id, prompt, context, expected_reply (optional), eval_hint (optional), category, pii_flag (Y/N)
   - ~2,000 rows preferred; if you only have 600-1,000 to start, we'll run a representative baseline and then expand.
   - Please anonymize obvious PII; mark pii_flag so we can apply redaction checks during ingestion.

2) Scoring & rubric mapping:
   - We'll run automatic metric: BLEU / ROUGE for surface overlap plus embedding-based semantic similarity (cosine on SBERT).
   - Mapping to your 3-point rubric: we will compute a continuous quality score 0-1 combining semantic similarity and a response-safety classifier; thresholds: >=0.8 -> OK, 0.5-0.8 -> Needs Edit, <0.5 -> Bad.
   - Human eval: sample 300 items stratified by category for rater validation. We'll provide an evaluation dashboard showing p50/p90/p99 latencies and quality distributions.

3) Recommended model shortlist (baseline run):
   - rw-open-7b-q8 (fast, quantized; good for cost-sensitive latency)
   - rw-open-13b (higher quality, slightly higher latency)
   - rw-instruct-13b-v2 (instruction-tuned variant; best-quality baseline for replies)

4) Prompt templates & prompt engineering notes:
   - We'll run 3 prompt templates: concise system prompt, conservative-safety prompt (to reduce hallucinations), and few-shot exemplars (3-shot) prompt. Please include any domain-specific phrasing you prefer in the prompt placeholders.

5) Sandbox provisioning & logs (Dev will confirm):
   - Sandbox: 7-day dedicated pool with autoscale off (to measure fixed-capacity latency).
   - We'll enable token-level logging with redaction hooks (we will not store raw PII-marked tokens; those will be hashed per your compliance request).

6) Timeline & deliverables:
   - On dataset receipt: 2 business days to ingest & validate, 3 business days to run baseline across the 3 models and generate the report + dashboard. Total ~5 business days after dataset validation.
   - Deliverables: evaluation report (PDF), interactive dashboard link, and a sandbox run summary (latency percentiles, throughput curves).

7) Next steps for you (Samir/Asha):
   - Share anonymized CSV and any preferred prompt wording.
   - Confirm any regulatory constraints around storing hashed PII for audit trails.

I'll start the baseline pipeline once we have the CSV. Ping me with any questions.

—Neha Kapoor
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexbank.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finexbank.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx Bank evals & Redwood setup — Sandbox & logs

Samir — quick note from infra: we can provision the 7-day sandbox as requested. Details: 

- Instance: Dedicated pool of 4x A100s (shared across their sandbox tests) with pinned model variants.
- Logging: we support token-level logs with configurable retention. For compliance, we can hash any token where pii_flag==Y at ingestion time; hashed tokens are stored separately and linked only by example_id for audit.
- Latency metrics: we capture p50/p90/p99 per model + per-prompt-template. We will provide CSV exports and a realtime dashboard.
- Access: Asha and Samir will get read-only dashboard links; Samir can request expanded access if your audit team needs raw hashed logs.

I'll start the provisioning once we confirm start date — Marissa, if FinEx wants to start Thursday 12/3, we can have resources ready by morning.

—Dev Patel
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
